catalog_quote: Word stress, here indicated by an acute accent on the stressed vowel, is usually carried by the penultimate syllable (áke, píla, turúa, golofíno). audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict' penultimate (rule 10 010 0010...) rests on the best available description, Hayami-Allen's 2001 Pittsburgh dissertation grammar (sec. 3.4, p.36), held as PDF with page-level scanned, and is independently corroborated by Watuseke 1991 note 9 (pp.242-243) and Voorhoeve's postscript 2.1 (p.241), both held; all quotations verified verbatim at the stated locators. sources.quote: Hayami-Allen 2001:36 (sec. 3.4): "The majority of native Ternatean words are disyllabic or longer. Most of them end with a vowel, and they all have penultimate stress. Words which are longer than three syllables have secondary stress on the fourth from the last syllable." Corroborated by Watuseke 1991:242-243 (note 9): "Word stress, here indicated by an acute accent on the stressed vowel, is usually carried by the penultimate syllable (ake, pila, turua, golofino).
